locator: I q.9 a.1 co.: Omne autem quod quocumque modo mutatur, est aliquo modo in potentia
interpretation: The first proof of God's immutability rests on the general principle that whatever is changed in any way is in some way in potency. Formalized only for changes of life in a duration frame: beginning or ceasing to live, and differing life-states at two times at which the thing lives, are changes quocumque modo. 'Aliquo modo in potentia' is read as potency in the subject (the InPotency of PureAct). Q.9 a.2 also admits mutability through a power in another (STMT-CREATURE-MUTABILITY-THROUGH-CREATOR-POWER); that wider sense is not this reading (DISAMB-POTENCY-IN-SUBJECT-VS-IN-ANOTHER). Aquinas elsewhere denies that creation is a change properly speaking; whether a being's first beginning to be counts under 'quocumque modo' is part of this reading's open burden, and the successionOnlyPrincipleInsufficient control shows the derivation needs it.
